title: Add playbook-lint CLI and simulated-exec sandbox for safe on-call verification
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: On-call runbooks and playbooks are frequently updated but we still see regressions where a runbook contains destructive or non-idempotent steps that lack mitigations. This PR introduces two utilities aimed at reducing human error during incident response: 1) playbook-lint: a static validator for runbook/playbook YAML (structure, required fields, de-escalation links, and hazard detection); 2) simulated-exec sandbox: a deterministic dry-run harness that executes playbook steps against a configurable mock backend to validate expected side-effects, timing, retries, and guard-clauses.

Goals: - Surface missing preconditions (rbac checks, required approvals) as lint errors. - Detect patterns that commonly cause harm (unescaped shell commands, operations without confirmation, use of broad wildcards, implicit timeouts). - Provide an integration point for incident-bot so new or changed playbooks are automatically linted and optionally dry-run in PR CI. - Keep the sandbox safe: no real network or system calls; all actions are resolved by a small, versioned simulation library with pluggable mocks.

What changed (single-string summary): Added a CLI (src/cli/playbook_lint.py) and a simulation harness (src/simexec/) with a library of common mocked actions, a JSON-based simulation registry, unit tests, docs, and a CI workflow that runs lint + smoke simulation on changed playbooks. Added an incident-bot hook that posts lint results and a simulated-exec report to PRs so reviewers can see what the dry-run would have done.

Checklist:
- [x] Parser for playbook YAML with schema validation (supports legacy and new schemas)
- [x] Rule engine for lint checks (configurable ruleset; SRE team can opt in/out)
- [x] Simulation harness with timeout and retry modelling
- [x] Example mocks for: cloud-cli, k8s-apply, secret-rotation, svc-restart
- [x] CI integration and GHA workflow update
- [x] Documentation and a short migration guide for existing playbooks

Backwards compatibility: playbook-lint supports both our legacy runbook YAML (v1) and the new structured step format (v2). Rules default to non-blocking; repository-level .playbook-lint.yml can promote specific rules to errors. The simulated-exec harness is opt-in via .simexec-config.yaml to avoid accidental runs during CI if a repo opts out.

Security & safety notes: The simexec runtime runs in a hermetic Python sandbox and resolves all actions to internal mocks. There are explicit assertions preventing any subprocess, socket, or filesystem mutation beyond a temporary test directory. The code includes a hardened white-list for action names and a CI policy that fails the workflow if an unknown action is encountered in a playbook.

Related: ENG-1248 (playbook quality initiative); SRE-76 (on-call safety checklist).

How to review: Start with unit tests under tests/simexec and the example playbooks in examples/playbooks/. Run the CLI locally against examples: python -m src.cli.playbook_lint examples/playbooks/incident_memory_leak.yaml --format=github. The simexec emulator can be invoked with --simulate to produce a trace.json that the incident-bot comment formatter understands.

Release notes: Adds playbook-lint CLI and simulated-exec sandbox to slo-toolkit. Integrates with incident-bot to surface lint and dry-run outputs in PRs. Opt-in simulation config via .simexec-config.yaml.

review_comments:
Ravi Patel: Nice work — can we add an explicit rule for 'no command with curl|wget without -s|--silent'? That pattern has bitten us.
Maya Chen: Added a hazard rule to detect common download patterns; flagged false positives are now suppressible via 'suppressions' metadata in the playbook. See updated tests.

Elena Gómez: The simexec mocks are great. Two safety requests: (1) ensure no shell expansion in mock payloads, (2) make CI fail on unknown actions.
Maya Chen: Implemented both; runner now rejects any action not present in simulation registry and test coverage added.

Tom Hsu: CI failed on first run due to flakey timeout in test_simexec when running on GitHub-hosted runners. Could we make the tests less timing-sensitive?
Maya Chen: Reworked timing assertions to be tolerant and added a deterministic clock for the harness. Rerun CI — green.

Ravi Patel: Suggest adding an example of migrating legacy v1 playbook to v2 with guard-clauses.
Maya Chen: Added examples/playbooks/legacy_to_v2_migration.md and linked in docs.
release_notes:
- Added playbook-lint CLI to statically validate runbooks
- Added simulated-exec sandbox for deterministic dry-runs in CI and locally
- Incident-bot integration posts lint + simexec trace to PRs
- Default behavior is non-blocking; project config can enforce stricter rules
